content.title: About
content.content: Dried blueberries are blueberries (Vaccinium corymbosum) that have been dehydrated to a low moisture level. They retain the characteristic sweet‑tart flavor, bright color, and most of the nutrients found in fresh berries.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Blueberries are considered a “superfood” because of their high antioxidant content, especially anthocyanins.
Dried blueberries store much longer than fresh ones—up to 12 months when kept properly.
In the United States, blueberries are primarily grown in Michigan, Oregon, and Washington, and the dried form is popular as a snack and baking ingredient.
Dried berries are often used in energy bars and granola mixes.
Blueberry is the state fruit of Michigan.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Dried blueberries contain anthocyanins that help combat free radicals and support cellular health.

items.title: Eye health support
items.content: Flavonoids in blueberries may improve night vision and reduce age‑related eye decline.

items.title: Vitamin C source
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: The natural sugars are concentrated, but dried blueberries still raise blood glucose slowly, which is beneficial for glucose control.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to berries of the cranberry family.

items.title: Sugar concentration
items.content: Drying concentrates natural sugars, so people monitoring sugar intake should watch portion size.

items.title: Added ingredients
items.content: Some manufacturers add sugar or preservatives; always check the ingredient list.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Dried blueberries can be eaten as a snack, added to oatmeal, yogurt, baked goods, salads, or used in energy bars. If a softer texture is desired, soak them in water for 10‑15 minutes before use.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For long‑term storage, keep them in the refrigerator or freezer. Discard any berries that show signs of mold or off‑odors.
